title: Welcome to Human Biology: What do you already know?

starterQuestions.q: What type of ribosomes do prokaryotes and eukaryotes possess?
starterQuestions.a: Prokaryotes possess 70S ribosomes; eukaryotes possess 80S ribosomes (and 70S within mitochondria/chloroplasts).

starterQuestions.q: Why is it scientifically inaccurate to say mitochondria 'produce energy'?
starterQuestions.a: Energy cannot be created or destroyed (First Law of Thermodynamics); mitochondria transfer chemical energy from respiratory substrates to synthesize ATP.

starterQuestions.q: Outline the sequential steps from gene to synthesized polypeptide.
starterQuestions.a: Nuclear transcription (DNA → mRNA) → mRNA export → Ribosomal translation (mRNA + tRNA) → ATP-dependent peptide bond formation.

starterQuestions.q: Identify 3 key structural differences between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.
starterQuestions.a: Prokaryotes lack a membrane-bound nucleus, lack membrane-bound organelles, have circular naked DNA/plasmids, and have peptidoglycan cell walls.

starterQuestions.q: What is the primary physiological function of epithelial tissue?
starterQuestions.a: Forms continuous protective barriers, lines cavities/tubes, and facilitates selective absorption, secretion, and transcellular transport.

terminology.def: Prokaryotes contain smaller 70S ribosomes; eukaryotes contain 80S cytosolic ribosomes and 70S in mitochondria.
